title: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe

questions.question: The French Revolution helped popularise the idea that sovereignty belongs to:
questions.explanation: Revolutionary ideas challenged dynastic rule and linked political authority to the nation.

questions.question: The Congress of Vienna in 1815 mainly sought to:
options: Restore conservative monarchies and the European balance of power
questions.explanation: The settlement attempted to restore conservative order after Napoleon’s defeat.

questions.question: The Zollverein was:
questions.explanation: The customs union reduced tariff barriers among many German states.

questions.question: Marianne became a symbol of:
options: The French nation and its republican values
questions.explanation: Marianne personified the French nation and ideas such as liberty.

questions.question: Nationalist tension in the Balkans grew partly because:
options: The region had no ethnic diversity
Different national groups and great-power interests competed as Ottoman authority weakened
questions.explanation: Competing national aspirations and outside powers made the region unstable.

questions.question: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 was opposed because it:
options: Allowed detention without trial under emergency powers
questions.explanation: The act extended repressive powers and was widely criticised as unjust.

questions.question: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in:
questions.explanation: British troops fired on a gathering at Amritsar on 13 April 1919.

questions.question: Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1922 after:
options: The Chauri Chaura incident turned violent
questions.explanation: After protesters killed policemen at Chauri Chaura, Gandhi called off the movement.

questions.question: The Salt March of 1930 protested against:
options: The use of the spinning wheel
The British salt tax and monopoly
questions.explanation: Salt was a shared necessity and the tax symbolised colonial exploitation.

questions.question: The idea of satyagraha emphasises:
questions.explanation: Satyagraha seeks to resist injustice through truth and non-violence.

title: The Making of a Global World

questions.question: The pre-modern Silk Routes connected:
options: Asian, European and African regions through trade and cultural exchange
questions.explanation: The routes carried goods, people, ideas and beliefs across regions.

questions.question: Indentured labour migration in the nineteenth century was closely linked to:
questions.explanation: Workers were recruited under contracts to plantations and other colonial enterprises.

questions.question: The Great Depression began around:
questions.explanation: The severe global economic downturn began in 1929.

questions.question: The Bretton Woods institutions included the:
questions.explanation: The IMF and World Bank emerged from the Bretton Woods conference arrangements.

questions.question: Globalisation in the historical chapter includes the movement of:
options: Goods, people, capital, technology and ideas
questions.explanation: Global connections formed through multiple kinds of movement and exchange.

questions.question: Proto-industrialisation refers to:
options: Production for markets before factories became widespread
The end of all household production
A type of farming without trade
questions.explanation: Merchant-controlled production often took place in rural households before the factory system spread.

questions.question: Merchants used rural households for production partly because:
options: Guild restrictions and demand for labour made dispersed production useful
questions.explanation: Merchant production outside towns could bypass some guild restrictions and use available rural labour.

questions.question: The factory system changed production by:
options: Bringing workers and machines together in one place
Removing the need for labour completely
questions.explanation: Factories concentrated machinery and workers under organised supervision.

questions.question: Why did handloom weavers sometimes continue despite factory competition?
options: Some markets valued variety, fine quality and flexibility
questions.explanation: Hand production could survive in specialised or changing markets.

questions.question: Industrial product advertisements often tried to:
options: Create demand and make products seem desirable or trustworthy
questions.explanation: Advertising helped shape consumer desire and brand recognition.

title: Print Culture and the Modern World

questions.question: Johann Gutenberg is associated with the development of:
options: The movable-type printing press in Europe
questions.explanation: Gutenberg’s press helped transform book production in Europe.

questions.question: Print helped the Protestant Reformation by:
options: Spreading reformist writings and enabling wider discussion
questions.explanation: Printed texts circulated arguments beyond small circles of readers.

questions.question: The growth of print culture encouraged:
options: New reading publics and wider circulation of ideas
questions.explanation: Printed material supported debate, reform and public discussion.

questions.question: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was intended mainly to:
questions.explanation: Colonial authorities used the act to curb criticism in vernacular newspapers.

questions.question: Women’s access to print in the nineteenth century contributed to:
options: Debates over education, social reform and women’s roles
An end to all domestic writing
The removal of every social barrier immediately
questions.explanation: Print made new arguments and experiences available and helped fuel debate.

questions.question: Sustainable development aims to:
options: Use resources without considering future generations
Meet present needs while protecting future needs and the environment
Replace every local resource with imports
questions.explanation: Sustainability balances development with long-term environmental and social needs.

questions.question: Which soil is commonly associated with cotton cultivation in the Deccan?
questions.explanation: Black soil retains moisture and is widely associated with cotton.

questions.question: Resource planning includes:
options: Identifying resources, developing suitable structures and matching plans to needs
questions.explanation: Planning connects resource availability with technology, institutions and equitable development.

questions.question: A major cause of soil erosion is:
questions.explanation: Removing vegetation and poor land management leave soil vulnerable to erosion.

questions.question: Which action supports sustainable resource use?
questions.explanation: Efficiency and reuse reduce pressure on natural resources.

questions.question: Biodiversity is important because it:
options: Has no role in ecosystem stability
Supports ecological balance and provides valuable resources
questions.explanation: Biodiversity supports ecosystem functioning and has ecological, economic and cultural value.

questions.question: A species at high risk of extinction is described as:
questions.explanation: Endangered species face a significant risk of extinction.

questions.question: The Chipko movement is remembered for:
questions.explanation: The movement mobilised people to resist tree felling and protect forests.

questions.question: Joint Forest Management involves:
options: Only private companies controlling all forests
Local communities participating in forest protection and management
Replacing forests with plantations in every case
questions.explanation: JFM links community participation with forest conservation and benefit-sharing.

questions.question: Why can protected areas alone be insufficient for conservation?
options: Local livelihoods and community stewardship also affect conservation outside boundaries
questions.explanation: Conservation often depends on broader landscapes and community cooperation.

questions.question: A multipurpose river project is designed to provide several benefits such as:
questions.explanation: Dams and river projects may serve multiple purposes, though they also have costs.

questions.question: Rooftop rainwater harvesting primarily helps to:
options: Collect rainwater for storage or groundwater recharge
Remove the need for water management
questions.explanation: Roof runoff can be stored or directed into recharge structures.

questions.question: One concern associated with large dams is:
options: Displacement of people and ecological changes
questions.explanation: Large projects can affect habitats, river flows and communities in the reservoir area.

questions.question: Water scarcity can occur even in regions with rainfall when:
options: Overuse, pollution, uneven distribution or poor storage limits usable water
questions.explanation: Scarcity can reflect access and management as well as physical availability.

questions.question: The Narmada Bachao Andolan raised concerns prominently about:
options: Large dams, displacement and environmental effects
questions.explanation: The movement drew attention to social and environmental consequences of dam projects.

questions.question: Rabi crops are generally sown in:
options: The same month in every climate
questions.explanation: Rabi crops are sown in winter and harvested in spring or early summer.

questions.question: Kharif crops are typically associated with:
questions.explanation: Kharif crops are sown with the monsoon and harvested later in the season.

questions.question: Rice generally requires:
questions.explanation: Rice is a warm-season crop with high water needs in many growing systems.

questions.question: Plantation agriculture is characterised by:
options: A single commercial crop grown on a large scale
questions.explanation: Plantations typically specialise in commercial crops over large areas.

questions.question: The Green Revolution in India is linked to:
options: High-yielding seeds, irrigation and increased use of farm inputs
The replacement of food grains with timber
questions.explanation: New seeds and supporting inputs raised yields especially in selected regions and crops.

questions.question: Iron ore is classified as a:
questions.explanation: Ferrous minerals contain iron or are associated with iron and steel production.

questions.question: Which is a non-renewable energy resource?
questions.explanation: Coal forms over geological timescales and is not replenished on a human timescale.

questions.question: Solar and wind energy are often promoted because they:
options: Can be replenished naturally and reduce reliance on fossil fuels
Always provide constant output at all times
questions.explanation: They are renewable, although their output varies and installations still have impacts.

questions.question: Conserving minerals is important because:
options: Many mineral deposits are finite and take geological time to form
Minerals cannot be used in industry
questions.explanation: Extraction depletes finite deposits, so efficient use and recycling matter.

questions.question: A major environmental concern associated with burning coal is:
questions.explanation: Coal combustion releases pollutants and carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Manufacturing contributes to development by:
options: Adding value to raw materials and creating jobs
questions.explanation: Manufacturing processes raw materials into higher-value goods and supports employment.

questions.question: Cotton textile mills often benefit from access to:
options: Raw cotton, labour, markets and transport
questions.explanation: Raw materials, labour, energy, transport and markets influence industrial location.

questions.question: Industrial pollution may affect:
options: Air, water, land and human health
questions.explanation: Emissions and waste can damage multiple environmental systems.

questions.question: Why are some industries located near ports?
options: Ports reduce transport costs for imported inputs and exported goods
Ports remove the need for electricity
questions.explanation: Ports can lower the cost of moving bulky inputs and finished products.

questions.question: Cleaner production can include:
options: Energy efficiency, waste treatment and recycling
questions.explanation: Pollution prevention and treatment reduce industrial impacts.

questions.question: For carrying heavy bulky goods over long distances on land, which mode is often efficient?
questions.explanation: Railways can move large volumes of freight efficiently over land.

questions.question: Pipelines are particularly useful for transporting:
options: Petroleum, gas and some liquid products
questions.explanation: Pipelines move fluids and gases continuously over long distances.

questions.question: The Golden Quadrilateral road project connects major metropolitan centres including:
options: Jaipur, Patna, Imphal and Shimla only
All state capitals in a single ring
questions.explanation: The highway network links Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata.

questions.question: International trade involves:
options: Exchange of goods and services between countries
questions.explanation: Imports and exports connect national economies.

questions.question: Tourism can support the economy by:
options: Creating employment and demand for local services
Guaranteeing that every region earns equally
questions.explanation: Tourism generates income and jobs but requires responsible management.

questions.question: Power sharing is desirable in a democracy because it:
options: Reduces conflict and respects diverse groups
Gives all power to one person
questions.explanation: Sharing can reduce social conflict and improve political legitimacy.

questions.question: Belgium’s approach to diversity included:
options: Giving all authority to one language group
Power sharing among linguistic communities and regions
questions.explanation: Belgium accommodated language communities through constitutional power-sharing arrangements.

questions.question: The majoritarian approach in Sri Lanka contributed to tension because it:
options: Gave equal recognition to all communities
Favoured the Sinhala majority and disadvantaged minorities
questions.explanation: Majoritarian measures deepened alienation among minority communities.

questions.question: Horizontal power sharing is among:
options: Political parties in an election only
questions.explanation: Horizontal sharing separates powers among branches of government.

questions.question: Vertical power sharing refers to division of power among:
options: The three branches at one level only
questions.explanation: Vertical sharing distributes authority between national, state and local levels.

questions.question: Federalism divides authority between:
options: A single ruler and private firms
Different levels of government under a constitutional arrangement
questions.explanation: A federation constitutionally allocates powers to more than one level of government.

questions.question: The Union List contains subjects that generally require:
questions.explanation: Defence and foreign affairs are examples of Union List subjects.

questions.question: The Concurrent List includes subjects on which:
options: Both Parliament and state legislatures can legislate, subject to constitutional rules
questions.explanation: Concurrent subjects are shared legislative responsibilities.

questions.question: The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments are associated with:
options: Local self-government in rural and urban areas
The creation of the Supreme Court
questions.explanation: The amendments strengthened Panchayati Raj and urban local bodies.

questions.question: A key feature of Indian federalism is:
options: Constitutionally defined powers and an independent judiciary
One language required for every citizen
questions.explanation: Constitutional division of powers and judicial interpretation support federalism.

questions.question: The idea of gender division as a social construct means that:
options: Many roles and expectations are shaped by society
Only law creates every family practice
questions.explanation: Social norms influence expectations about work, leadership and behaviour.

questions.question: Communalism becomes dangerous when:
options: Religion is used to claim political dominance or portray communities as enemies
questions.explanation: Communal politics treats religious identity as a basis for hostility or unequal power.

questions.question: A secular state should:
options: Promote only one religion as the state religion
Treat citizens equally regardless of religion
questions.explanation: Secularism protects religious freedom while avoiding state discrimination.

questions.question: Caste can influence politics when:
options: Groups mobilise around representation, interests or discrimination
questions.explanation: Caste identities may shape mobilisation, representation and debates about equality.

questions.question: A democratic response to social inequality emphasises:
options: Equal rights, dignity and protection from discrimination
questions.explanation: Democracy should protect equal citizenship and human dignity.

questions.question: A major function of political parties is to:
options: Contest elections and present policy choices
questions.explanation: Parties organise candidates, offer programmes and compete for public support.

questions.question: The party or coalition that commands a legislative majority usually:
questions.explanation: A majority in the legislature enables formation of the government.

questions.question: One challenge faced by political parties is:
options: Limited internal democracy and concentration of leadership
Too much direct decision-making by every citizen
questions.explanation: Internal democracy and concentration of power are common concerns.

questions.question: An opposition party can help democracy by:
options: Scrutinising government actions and offering alternatives
questions.explanation: Opposition oversight promotes accountability and debate.

questions.question: A reform intended to improve party democracy could be:
options: Secretly selecting every leader without consultation
Transparent candidate selection and regular internal elections
questions.explanation: Transparency and internal participation can strengthen party accountability.

questions.question: An important expected outcome of democracy is:
options: A guarantee that all problems disappear
questions.explanation: Democracy provides mechanisms for accountability, though outcomes still vary.

questions.question: Democracy is associated with dignity because it:
options: Treats some citizens as permanently inferior
Recognises political equality and gives people a voice
questions.explanation: Equal citizenship and participation can support dignity and rights.

questions.question: A democratic government may take time to decide because:
options: Consultation, debate and procedures require time
questions.explanation: Democratic decision-making includes discussion and institutional checks.

questions.question: Which statement about economic inequality in democracies is most accurate?
options: Democratic equality does not by itself guarantee equal wealth
questions.explanation: Political equality can coexist with substantial economic inequality.

questions.question: A useful measure of democratic success includes:
options: Only the size of the capital city
Only the speed of every decision
questions.explanation: Democratic outcomes involve both processes and how governments respond to citizens.

questions.question: Per capita income is calculated as:
questions.explanation: Per capita income is average income per person.

questions.question: Different people may have different development goals because:
options: Their circumstances, priorities and values differ
questions.explanation: Development goals depend on people’s lives and what they value.

questions.question: Public facilities such as schools and hospitals matter because:
options: They improve access to essential services and quality of life
They have no effect on development
questions.explanation: Health, education and other services contribute directly to well-being.

questions.question: Sustainable development requires attention to:
options: Long-term resource use and environmental limits
questions.explanation: Development should not compromise future generations’ ability to meet needs.

questions.question: The Human Development Index considers indicators including:
options: Rainfall, road length and exports only
questions.explanation: HDI combines indicators of life expectancy, education and income.

questions.question: Agriculture belongs to the:
questions.explanation: Primary activities obtain or produce natural-resource-based goods.

questions.question: Converting cotton into cloth is an activity in the:
questions.explanation: Manufacturing transforms raw materials into goods.

questions.question: Transport and banking are examples of:
questions.explanation: They provide services rather than directly extracting or manufacturing goods.

questions.question: Disguised unemployment occurs when:
options: More people work than needed, so some workers add little or no extra output
Every worker is paid a high salary
questions.explanation: Removing some workers would not significantly reduce total production.

questions.question: MGNREGA was designed to provide:
options: A legal guarantee of wage employment for rural households meeting the conditions
questions.explanation: The act guarantees a specified amount of rural wage employment subject to eligibility and terms.

questions.question: Money solves the barter problem known as:
questions.explanation: Barter requires each party to want exactly what the other offers.

questions.question: Collateral is:
options: An asset pledged as security for a loan
questions.explanation: The lender may claim collateral if the borrower defaults, subject to the agreement and law.

questions.question: Formal sources of credit include:
questions.explanation: Banks and cooperatives are formal credit institutions.

questions.question: Self-help groups can improve access to credit by:
options: Pooling savings and supporting members’ borrowing
questions.explanation: SHGs encourage savings and can facilitate loans for members.

questions.question: The Reserve Bank of India supervises:
options: The formal banking system and aspects of credit regulation
questions.explanation: The RBI regulates and supervises important parts of India’s banking and monetary system.

questions.question: A multinational corporation (MNC) is a company that:
options: Owns or controls production in more than one country
questions.explanation: MNCs organise production and investment across national borders.

questions.question: Foreign trade can connect markets by:
options: Allowing goods and services to be bought and sold across countries
questions.explanation: Imports and exports link producers and consumers in different economies.

questions.question: Liberalisation generally refers to:
options: Removing or reducing certain restrictions on economic activity and trade
questions.explanation: Liberalisation reduces selected controls and trade barriers.

questions.question: The World Trade Organization is associated with:
options: Rules and negotiations concerning international trade
questions.explanation: The WTO administers trade agreements and provides a forum for trade negotiations.

questions.question: Fair globalisation seeks to:
options: Spread benefits more widely and protect vulnerable workers and communities
questions.explanation: Fair globalisation focuses on inclusion, labour standards and sharing gains more equitably.

questions.question: A consumer’s right to information includes details about:
options: Price, quantity, quality and relevant product information
questions.explanation: Consumers need accurate information to make informed choices.

questions.question: A quality certification mark such as ISI may help consumers identify:
questions.explanation: Certification marks signal compliance with specified standards for covered products.

questions.question: A bill or receipt is useful because it:
options: Records the purchase and can support a complaint or warranty claim
Has no legal or practical value
questions.explanation: Purchase records can help establish transaction details in a dispute.

questions.question: A consumer complaint should normally include:
options: Evidence, transaction details and the issue being raised
questions.explanation: A clear complaint with records is easier to assess and resolve.

questions.question: Consumer protection matters because:
options: Consumers may face misleading claims, unsafe products or unfair practices
questions.explanation: Consumer rights and remedies help address information gaps and unfair conduct.
